item.text:
Deep-sea mining cannot be guaranteed to end battery-metal shortages. These drafts advocate for it without presenting that prediction as fact.

### (a) Three posts

1. We support commercial deep-sea mining to expand battery-metal supplies. We need more sources, stronger supply chains and a strategy that tackles shortages head-on.

2. We want battery-metal shortages solved—not accepted as inevitable. Commercial deep-sea mining belongs in our supply strategy, alongside recycling and responsible production on land.

3. We back a broader supply of battery metals. That means advancing commercial deep-sea mining with enforceable environmental safeguards, transparent oversight and accountability.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 108 words

We refuse to accept battery-metal shortages as a permanent constraint on progress. We support developing commercial deep-sea mining as an additional source of the materials that power batteries, alongside stronger recycling systems and responsible production on land. Our objective is clear: abundant, reliable supplies that keep essential technologies moving forward. We want a supply strategy built around more sources, not continued dependence on a narrow set of producers. That means establishing enforceable environmental safeguards, demanding transparent oversight and holding operators accountable. We stand for confronting shortages with investment and action—and we believe commercial deep-sea mining deserves a place in that effort.
